_guidance: Copy to modules/<module>/PlanningContracts/UC-nn-nn.planning.json and delete every _guidance key. The sections below are exactly those the Use Case Format defines for Planning Contract — Intent, Plan, Operations with their Parameters and their Returns and errors, Planning rules, Reversal, Resolved plans. Do not add others. Where no plan should ever be produced, set planned to false, fill notPlanned, and leave contracts empty.

useCase.name: Copy the name verbatim from the use case file — the validator warns when the two drift.

_guidance_notPlanned: Present only when planned is false. Then contracts must be empty.

notPlanned.reason: One line. Why no plan can ever exist here.
requestsThatArriveHere: Requests a router will nonetheless send this way.

requestsThatArriveHere.gloss: write the Roman Urdu ones too

routeInsteadTo.goesTo: Intent name, use case ID, or a plain statement that it is not offered

intent.name: noun.verb
intent.summary: One or two sentences: what the plan does and how many steps it takes.
routesHere: Real requests, in the words someone would actually use.

routesHere.text: Roman Urdu mein bhi likho — daftar isi tarah baat karta hai
routesHere.gloss: write them in Roman Urdu too — this is how the office speaks

plan._guidance: Ordered steps, executed unconditionally. Inputs are resolvable references — $request.x, $session.x, $stepN.x — or literals. The controller substitutes and calls; it evaluates no conditions. Validation, permission, duplicate and capacity checks belong to the API and arrive as errors; the plan does not test for them beforehand.
plan.onFailure: The controller stops and reports. Name what the API enforces rather than the plan.
plan.atomicity: What has been written when the run stops part way — including anything a read writes, such as an audit entry.

operations.name: operation.name
operations._guidance_idempotencyKey: Required for a non-idempotent write. Name the fields that make the request unique.
operations.purpose: What it is for, in one sentence.

parameters.name: field
parameters._guidance_source: request = the instruction supplied it. session = controller context supplies it and it may never be read from the request, even where the request names a branch or a year. step = an earlier response supplies it. literal = fixed in the plan.
parameters.notes: Constraints, and what must never be put here.

parameters.name: some_entity_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse, or ask. The plan never ran, so nothing is written.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates. Never pick one.

parameters.notes: An entity id the parameter resolver obtains through the gateway's resolve door. Never write a lookup step into the plan — the validator rejects any capability named *.resolve or *.lookup.

fields.name: field
fields.description: A later step may reference this as $stepN.field.

errors._guidance_mapsTo: The E-id in the use case that defines this failure. null where none does — the validator warns, which is the signal to add one.
errors.written: What has been written when this arrives.
errors.note: How the controller should report it.

operations.writesOnRead: Only where a read nevertheless writes something — an audit entry, for example.

planningRules.rule: Name the mistake. 'Wire section_id from the section field, never from the class field' beats 'be careful with ids'.
planningRules._guidance_derivedFrom: Ids in the use case this rule follows from, and System Conventions it applies. The validator checks each one still exists.

reversal.statement: The operation that undoes the write, or a plain statement that none exists, so the controller does not attempt a compensating call of its own.

request.text: Aik asli request, jaise daftar mein kahi jati hai
request.gloss: A real request, as it would be said in the office

resolvedPlans.context: The session context this run assumes — role, branch, academic session.
resolvedPlans.outcome: The outcome of a clean run, in the school's own terms.
